e1758c1ce1f18eb8.text: Tuesday afternoon, Priya in Support sent us a screenshot. A customer had waited so long for our assistant to reply that they'd started talking to themselves.

a779106176ebe8cc.text: Ten minutes later, Jonas in Finance replied on the same thread. He didn't care why it was slow. He wanted to know what it cost, per request, so he can split our bill by team.

423e1c677e9c782d.text: That one request went through our gateway, out to a model, into the vector store and into a cache. Four services, four sets of logs, and Tomasz spent an hour scrolling through them.

3163d3443d8db612.text: And guessing won't do. If we blame the wrong part, someone spends a week speeding up the wrong thing. If we hand Finance a hunch, it ends up in a budget.

312f785207c20872.text: Here's the good news. That request was traced from start to finish, so every step it took was written down on one timeline, with how long it ran and notes about what it did.

2e7da4c8b70db8f2.text: You see it as a waterfall. One bar per step, each step tucked under the one that called it, every bar with its own clock and its own notes. Everything we need is in there.

cb975d69ca1b4379.text: Here's your part. Find the step that took longest, not counting the whole request. Work out how many tokens the model calls used in total. And find what the cache lookup sits under.

6cf2a964e7c4d2e5.text: And please don't tell me what it looks like. Read it off the trace, write the numbers down, and we'll give Priya and Jonas a proper answer.
